_comment: Branch protection for the one branch this repository has.
Applied by hand with the standards repository's scripts/apply-rulesets.sh,
matched BY NAME, so editing this file and re-running updates the ruleset
in place rather than creating a second one.
TWO RULES, AND THE ABSENCES ARE THE DESIGN.
NO pull_request RULE. This repository takes DIRECT PUSHES and opens no
pull requests: that is the whole distribution contract, and every other
repository in the fleet receives its files the same way. A pull-request
rule here would forbid the only way work lands, and it would do it in the
most expensive shape available: the push is rejected at the server with a
message about protection, not a message about policy, and the release
workflow's own commit is rejected along with it.
NO required_status_checks RULE. Required checks are a MERGE-TIME gate:
they stop collaborators merging a pull request. There are no merges here,
so there is nothing for them to gate. (The one sentence that reads as
'blocks direct pushes' belongs to a different feature, Require workflows
to pass, which is organization-only, and this account is a User.) They
also carry a trap: a required check that nothing can report leaves every
pull request PENDING rather than failed, and the check-name contract has
already drifted once across this fleet.
What survives is what actually protects the branch from an accident that
cannot be undone: deletion, and a force push that discards history.
THE BYPASS IS THE HUMAN ADMIN ONLY. actor_id 5 is the repository-admin
role, not github-actions. A rule with no bypass at all is the shape that
is demonstrably not enforced on this account anyway, so the honest choice
is a rule that works over a rule that lies.
~DEFAULT_BRANCH is GitHub's own selector, resolved per repository, so this
keeps working across a branch rename. Development means TRUNK here; the
name is inherited convention, not a promotion stage.
name: Protect the default branch
